name: Sarma
description: Fermented (sour) cabbage leaves rolled around a seasoned ground meat and rice filling, slow-simmered until tender. A staple of Balkan winter and holiday tables.
ingredients: 200g smoked bacon or ribs (optional, for extra flavor)
steps: Sauté the diced onion in oil until translucent, then mix with the ground meat, rice, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Layer the rolls in a large pot, tucking smoked meat between layers if using.
Mix tomato paste with water and pour over the rolls until just covered.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2-3 hours, until the cabbage is fully tender and the flavors meld.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate only — actual values vary with meat fat content and rolling size.

name: Ćevapi
description: Small grilled minced-meat rolls, a Balkan grill staple, traditionally served with flatbread (somun/lepinja), raw onion, and ajvar.
steps: Knead the ground meat with salt, pepper, garlic, and baking soda until slightly sticky and well combined.
Rest the mixture in the fridge for at least a few hours, ideally overnight.
Shape into small finger-sized rolls, about 7-10cm long.
Grill over high heat, turning frequently, until well-charred outside and cooked through (about 8-10 minutes total).
Serve hot with flatbread, chopped raw onion, and ajvar.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate for the meat only (5-6 pieces), not including bread or sides.

name: Ajvar
description: A rich relish made from roasted red bell peppers and eggplant, slow-cooked with oil and garlic. Served as a condiment or spread.
steps: Roast the peppers and eggplant over an open flame or under a broiler until the skins blister and blacken.
Let them steam under a covered bowl for 15 minutes, then peel off the skins and seeds.
Finely chop or grind the roasted flesh.
Cook the mixture slowly in oil over low heat, stirring often, for 45-60 minutes until thickened and deep red.
Stir in garlic, vinegar, and salt near the end, then jar while hot.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate per 2-tbsp (~30g) serving; oil content varies significantly by recipe.

name: Pljeskavica
description: A large, flat grilled patty of seasoned ground meat, often called the 'Balkan burger', served in flatbread with toppings.
steps: Combine ground meat with grated onion, garlic, salt, pepper, and baking soda.
Knead well and rest in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Shape into 4 large, flat patties about 1.5cm thick.
Grill over high heat, about 5-6 minutes per side, until well charred and cooked through.
Serve in flatbread with kajmak, ajvar, and chopped onion.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate for the patty only (~200g), not including bread or toppings.

name: Burek
description: A baked pastry of thin phyllo layers filled with seasoned ground meat, coiled or layered into a round pan.
steps: Sauté the onion with the ground meat until browned, season with salt and pepper, and let cool.
Brush each phyllo sheet lightly with oil, spread a thin layer of filling, and roll loosely into a coil.
Arrange the coils spiral-fashion in a round, oiled baking pan.
Brush the top with an oil-and-sparkling-water mixture for a crisp finish.
Bake at 200°C (390°F) for 35-40 minutes until deep golden and crisp.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate per generous slice (~150g); pastry oil content varies by baker.

name: Gibanica
description: A layered phyllo pastry with a savory custard of eggs, cheese, and yogurt poured between crumpled sheets, baked until puffed and golden.
steps: Whisk together eggs, yogurt, oil, and sparkling water.
Crumple each phyllo sheet loosely and layer into an oiled baking pan, sprinkling crumbled cheese between layers.
Pour the egg mixture evenly over the layered phyllo, making sure it soaks through.
Let it rest for 10-15 minutes so the liquid absorbs.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 35-40 minutes until puffed and golden brown.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate per slice (~150g); cheese saltiness/fat content varies.

name: Karađorđeva Šnicla
description: A rolled and breaded veal or pork cutlet stuffed with kajmak (or cream cheese), fried until golden, named after Serbian revolutionary leader Karađorđe.
ingredients: 4 large veal or pork cutlets, pounded thin
steps: Season the pounded cutlets with salt and pepper.
Place a spoonful of kajmak in the center of each cutlet and roll tightly, securing with a toothpick if needed.
Dredge each roll in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry at 175°C (350°F) until golden brown and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes.
Traditionally served with tartar sauce and fries.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate for one stuffed cutlet, fried; frying oil absorption varies.

name: Prebranac
description: Slow-baked white beans layered with generous amounts of caramelized onion — a beloved vegetarian winter dish.
steps: Cook the soaked beans in fresh water until just tender, reserving some cooking liquid.
Sauté the sliced onions in oil until deeply golden and caramelized.
Layer beans and caramelized onions in a baking dish, seasoning each layer with paprika, salt, and pepper.
Add a splash of the reserved bean liquid and bay leaves.
Bake uncovered at 180°C (350°F) for 45-60 minutes until the top is browned.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate per generous bowl (~300g); oil quantity varies by household.

name: Musaka
description: A layered bake of thinly sliced potatoes and seasoned ground meat, topped with an egg-and-yogurt custard and baked until set.
ingredients: Salt, pepper, and paprika to taste
steps: Fry the potato slices lightly in oil until just golden at the edges.
Sauté the onion with the ground meat, season with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Layer potatoes and meat alternately in a greased baking dish, finishing with a potato layer.
Whisk eggs with yogurt and pour evenly over the top.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 40-45 minutes until the top is set and golden.

name: Punjene Paprike
description: Bell peppers stuffed with a ground meat and rice filling, simmered in a light tomato sauce.
ingredients: 8-10 medium bell peppers, tops removed and cored
steps: Mix ground meat with rice, diced onion, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Stuff each pepper about three-quarters full with the mixture.
Stand the peppers upright in a pot and pour the tomato sauce around and over them.
Add enough water to nearly cover the peppers.
Simmer covered on low heat for about 1 hour, until the peppers are tender and rice is cooked through.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate for 2 stuffed peppers with sauce.

name: Đuveč
description: A baked casserole of rice, mixed vegetables, and often chunks of meat, seasoned with paprika — a colorful summer favorite.
steps: Brown the meat cubes in a bit of oil, then set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion and peppers until softened.
Combine meat, sautéed vegetables, rice, tomatoes, zucchini, paprika, salt, and pepper in a baking dish.
Pour in stock or water until the rice is just covered.
Cover and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 45-50 minutes, until the rice is tender and liquid absorbed.

name: Pasulj
description: A hearty bean stew, often cooked with smoked meat, paprika, and root vegetables — classic Balkan comfort food.
ingredients: 150g smoked pork ribs or bacon (optional, omit for vegetarian)
steps: Cook the soaked beans with the smoked meat in fresh water until beans are nearly tender.
In a separate pan, sauté onion and carrot in oil, stir in paprika and flour to make a light roux.
Stir the roux into the bean pot to thicken the broth.
Simmer for another 30-40 minutes until the beans are fully tender and the stew has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate per bowl (~350g) including smoked meat; vegetarian version is lower in fat/protein.

name: Šopska Salata
description: A fresh salad of chopped tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, and peppers, topped generously with grated white cheese.
steps: Combine diced tomatoes, cucumbers, pepper, and onion in a large bowl.
Dress with olive oil, vinegar, and a pinch of salt, tossing gently.
Divide onto plates and top generously with grated white cheese.
Serve immediately as a starter or side.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate per plate (~250g including cheese topping).

name: Palačinke
description: Thin, delicate crepes, typically filled with jam, Nutella-style spread, walnuts, or cheese, and rolled or folded.
ingredients: Butter or oil for the pan
Jam, chocolate spread, or ground walnuts for filling
steps: Whisk flour, milk, eggs, sugar, and salt into a smooth, thin batter.
Heat a lightly buttered non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour a thin layer of batter, swirling to coat the pan, and cook about 1 minute per side.
Spread the warm crepe with your filling of choice and roll or fold.
Repeat with remaining batter; serve warm, dusted with powdered sugar if desired.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate for 2 plain crepes with a light jam filling; chocolate/walnut fillings add calories.

name: Kremšnita
description: A classic Balkan/Central European dessert of two layers of flaky puff pastry sandwiching a thick vanilla custard, dusted with powdered sugar.
ingredients: 2 sheets puff pastry, baked flat and crisp
200ml heavy cream, whipped (optional, for a lighter custard)
steps: Bake the puff pastry sheets flat between trays until golden and crisp; let cool.
Whisk egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch, then temper with warmed milk.
Cook the mixture over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened into a custard.
Fold in vanilla (and whipped cream, if using) once slightly cooled.
Spread the custard over one pastry sheet, top with the second sheet, chill for several hours, then cut into squares.

nutritionPerServing.note: Estimate per square slice (~120g) of a 9-serving batch.
